checks.finding:
**1. The Windows twin of a changed function was missed, so `DirEntry::metadata()` errors carry depth on Unix and not on Windows.**

The diff adds depth to `DirEntryRaw::metadata_internal` only in the `#[cfg(not(windows))]` copy (`crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:297-306`). The `#[cfg(windows)]` copy right above it (`crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:287-295`) still ends in `.map_err(|err| Error::Io(io::Error::from(err)).with_path(&self.path))`, with no `with_depth`. The PR did update the Windows copies of `from_entry_os` (`:337-346`) and `from_path` (`:387-394`), so this one reads as an oversight rather than a choice.

Case: on Windows, `WalkBuilder::new(root).follow_links(true).build_parallel()`, a symlink at depth 2 whose target disappears after the entry is built (`from_path` with `link = true` sets `follow_link`, so `metadata_internal` stats again). `dent.metadata().unwrap_err().depth()` is `Some(2)` on Linux and macOS at HEAD and `None` on Windows. Fix: add `.with_depth(self.depth)` to the Windows `map_err` the same way as `:305`.
checks.evidence: Read, not run (no Windows host). On HEAD, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:297-306 (#[cfg(not(windows))] metadata_internal) now ends in `.map_err(|err| { Error::Io(err).with_depth(self.depth).with_path(&self.path) })`, while the #[cfg(windows)] twin at walk.rs:287-295 still ends in `.map_err(|err| Error::Io(io::Error::from(err)).with_path(&self.path))`; `git diff base...HEAD` shows the diff touched only the non-Windows copy, though it did update the Windows from_entry_os (:343-344) and from_path (:393-394). Error::depth() (crates/ignore/src/lib.rs:252-258) returns Some only through a WithDepth node, so on Windows a follow_link stat failure in DirEntryRaw::metadata returns depth() == None while Unix returns Some(depth). `git blame -L 287,295` puts the Windows lines at base commit a5ba50c, but the Unix/Windows asymmetry is created by this diff (at base neither copy carried depth), so it is a case the PR's stated change misses rather than a pre-existing defect.

checks.finding:
**2. Depth is now attached twice in `from_entry` and the Windows `from_entry_os`.**

Both sites already wrapped the error in `Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(err) }` at base, so `Error::depth()` already returned `Some(depth)` there. The diff adds an inner `.with_depth(depth)` without dropping the outer wrapper, so the error is now `WithDepth { WithPath { WithDepth { Io } } }`:

- `crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:331-332` (`from_entry`, `ent.file_type()`)
- `crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:344-345` (Windows `from_entry_os`, `ent.metadata()`)

Nothing a caller can observe through `depth()` changes at these two sites; only the nesting gets deeper. The base commit (`c10f151`, "ignore: always include depth in errors") warns that callers down-casting nested errors could break, and this adds a third layer for no gain. Either revert these two hunks, or keep the inner `with_depth` and delete the outer `Error::WithDepth { .. }` line so the shape matches the other sites in this diff and `Error::from_walkdir` (`crates/ignore/src/lib.rs:297-303`).
checks.evidence: Read, not run. On HEAD, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:331-332 (from_entry) and :344-345 (Windows from_entry_os) read `let err = Error::Io(err).with_depth(depth).with_path(ent.path()); Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(err) }`. with_depth (crates/ignore/src/lib.rs:269-271) builds `Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(self) }`, so the result is WithDepth{WithPath{WithDepth{Io}}}; at base the same lines were `Error::Io(io::Error::from(err)).with_path(ent.path())` under the same outer WithDepth, i.e. WithDepth{WithPath{Io}}. Error::depth() (lib.rs:252-258) returns Some(depth) at the outermost WithDepth in both versions, so the observable depth is unchanged and only nesting grows. git blame shows lines 331 and 344 come from the PR commit 4bb614d; the outer WithDepth lines 332/345 predate base (a5ba50c). Base commit c10f151's message does warn about callers down-casting nested errors, and Error::from_walkdir (lib.rs:296-303) uses the single WithPath{WithDepth{Io}} shape the finding cites.
